experiment: KEYSPEC v2 Private-Letter Splitting on the Z-Consistent (2db75746, 6,718 Rules) {5,6,7} World

v1_baseline.description: Standard KEYSPEC v1 unsplit receiver rows (110,087 R7 rows, 0 split receivers, 115,702-117,073 deduplicated rows)

v2_diff_vs_orig_w6_w7.description: KEYSPEC v2 splitting on w6 and w7 positions where 6,718 widened masks relative to 9,326 (split into m_orig vs diff classes in {5}, {6}, B)

v2_w6_split5_all.description: KEYSPEC v2 binary splitting {5} vs {6,7,8,9} at all link-6 vertices whose mask contains both 5 and {6,7,8,9}

v2_w6_56B_w7_diff.description: KEYSPEC v2 full 3-class splitting {5} (1), {6} (2), B={7,8,9} (28) at all link-6 vertices + diff splitting at link-7 vertices

key_conclusions: 1. KEYSPEC v2 full class splitting (v2_w6_56B_w7_diff, 2,599,525 R7 branch rows) reduces t* on the 6,718-rule Z-consistent {5,6,7} world from 0.010776039 to 0.009200106 (on 151 keys) and from 0.010102785 to 0.007423699 (with Kill B + H05 + all keys).

2. Comparing v2_w6_56B_w7_diff (t* = 0.009200106 on 151 keys; 0.007423699 with Kill B + H05 + all keys) against the Wave 4 hybrid benchmark Base=6718, Pic=Orig (t* = 0.009204094 on 151 keys; 0.007410588 with Kill B + H05 + all keys) proves that KEYSPEC v2 private-letter splitting eliminates 99.5% to 100% of the IN-slot mask-widening penalty (0.002679 out of 0.002692)!

3. Why does t* stop at 0.007423699 (matching Base=6718, Pic=Orig = 0.007410588)? Because on the p_i = 5 split branch (priv[i] = (1,)), M(7, ..., 1) equals h(7, wr, sr, p=5, sl, wl, ar, al), which is a pure base-row 6-wheel transfer via mrowR2 + cons2, and in KEYSPEC v1/v2, OUT slots (7 -> w_i) do not see priv[i] (so no existing EDGE rule can send negative charge specifically out of the p_i = 5 branch of R7 without also charging the p_i in {6,7} branches).
